publication_policy: Historical original-source evidence ONLY; no email events, camera coordinates or current contract changes automatically inferred.

sources.title: Sacramento County Flock ALPR installation environmental filing
sources.summary: California CEQA registry posts a Sacramento County notice of exemption for a Flock ALPR installation project on behalf of the Sheriff's Office. It documents a proposed site project, not installation completion, current uptime or a complete camera inventory.
sources.provider: California Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation, CEQAnet
open_questions: Was the installation actually completed and activated?
Where are the currently applicable Sheriff's Flock access and retention policies?

sources.title: Sacramento Sheriff published ALPR General Order, revision 4/16
sources.summary: Department PDF general order describes a maximum two-year retention period and LEARN sharing under the historical Car Detector/LEARN system. Its 'Rev 4/16' imprint is not proof of the current Flock contract, setting or 2026 policy; month-only imprint, day not authenticated.
sources.proof: Six-page agency General Order, stamped 10/12 (Rev 4/16), pages 1 and 5 visually reviewed
open_questions: Does the Sheriff have a current Flock-specific ALPR policy?
Did the historical LEARN sharing and two-year retention rules change?

sources.title: Cleveland ordinance authorizes Flock ALPR license and maintenance contracting
sources.summary: City Council Legistar records emergency Ordinance 683-2026 as passed July 15, 2026, effective August 15, authorizing the public safety director to enter one or more Flock annual license/maintenance contracts. Authorization is not proof of a later signed agreement or specific cameras.
sources.proof: Ordinance 683-2026; official action status Passed; adoption 2026-07-15
open_questions: Was a signed license or maintenance agreement later executed?
What amount was actually spent and what were its sharing terms?

sources.title: El Paso Council consideration of restrictions on new fixed-network ALPR agreements
sources.summary: Official Legistar history lists an October 13 City Council approval of the motion concerning restrictions on new fixed ALPR contracts; item header still says Agenda Ready and has no final action date. Treat the council action as reported, with unresolved header conflict, not proof of executed cancellations.
sources.provider: City of El Paso City Council
sources.proof: Item 26-1092, October 13 history row Approve / Pass; status header Agenda Ready
open_questions: Does the signed resolution or final City Council minutes reconcile the status-header discrepancy?
Did any existing vendor agreement actually terminate?

sources.title: Saint Paul Council adopts resolution calling to end Flock contracts
sources.summary: Resolution RES 26-1421 was adopted by City Council August 26, asking city administration and Ramsey County partners to end contracts, refrain from expansion and report back. Its official status reads Passed Unsigned by Mayor. Resolution is a call, not proof any contract was terminated or cameras removed.
sources.proof: RES 26-1421 Council Adopted / Pass; unsigned-by-mayor status
open_questions: Did the city administration terminate any agreements after the resolution?
Was the requested 60-day implementation report delivered?

sources.title: Allentown authorizes independent review and Flock LPR advisory subscription
sources.summary: Legistar resolution 31307 passed September 16 for a $10,000 single-source professional-service contract with IPVM for research and Flock LPR advisory services. The vendor is IPVM, not Flock; do not count $10,000 as Flock camera procurement or the adoption of a policy.
sources.amount_basis: City-council-authorized IPVM advisory service expenditure, NOT a Flock vendor agreement
open_questions: Did the independent review produce a publicly released assessment?
What agreements or camera systems were later approved, if any?

sources.title: Carrollton Council passes Flock IP-camera agreement authorization item
sources.summary: Council Legistar status Passed on a proposed cooperative agreement for lease of 82 Flock IP cameras and supporting software. The stated proposed cap is $398,258.34 annually and $1,194,775.02 total; the council listing is not independent proof of execution or installations, and these are IP cameras, not necessarily ALPR devices.
sources.amount_basis: Proposed three-year maximum in council-approved item; signed expenditure not established
sources.proof: Item 7749, official Legistar status Passed, agenda/final action 2026-09-15
open_questions: Was a final agreement signed and what was paid?
Which of the described IP cameras are actually ALPR readers?

sources.title: Rockford Council passes $443,998.16 Flock sole-source award
sources.summary: Council Legistar lists sole-source Flock award for $443,998.16 over one year, with three one-year extension options. History shows March 2 adoption after February 17 layover. This is the council's award action, not proof each option was exercised or an operational inventory.
sources.amount_basis: Council award amount, one year; additional options NOT presumed exercised
open_questions: Was the approved vendor contract signed and what equipment was delivered?
Were any of the three one-year options exercised?

sources.title: Monterey County Flock proposal for 63 LPR subscriptions through 2036
sources.summary: Board of Supervisors agenda requests negotiation authorization for a non-standard Flock agreement covering 63 LPR camera subscriptions with proposed $1,701,000 ten-year ceiling. Agenda status Scheduled PM, blank final action. Do not claim execution or adoption.
sources.amount_basis: Agenda proposal for September 2026 through August 2036, NOT an executed contract
sources.proof: Item A 26-368, Scheduled PM, no final action
open_questions: Did the Board ultimately approve or execute the proposed agreement?
How does the 63-camera proposal reconcile with the separately proposed 103-camera item?

sources.title: Manteca proposed Flock Condor contract amendment
sources.summary: City agenda proposes amendment to the prior Flock agreement for six Condor cameras, additional annual $18,000 and installation $1,500, total increase not to exceed $55,500. Item status Agenda Ready, blank final action. Condor cameras should not be counted as ALPR camera GPS points.
sources.amount_basis: Proposed contract increase, NOT independently verified enacted
sources.proof: Item 26-399, agenda August 18, no adopted action in header
open_questions: Did City Council adopt the amendment?
Were the Condor devices installed, and are any of them ALPR readers?

sources.title: South San Francisco staff recommends new fixed ALPR vendor RFP
sources.summary: October 28 staff report recommends directing staff to draft a vendor RFP by January 2027 and return with an evaluation by April 2027. The report says the department has contracted with Flock since November 2022. Agenda status is Agenda Ready; no final action recorded, so no vendor switch or RFP authorization is claimed.
open_questions: Did Council authorize a vendor RFP?
What vendor, if any, did a later evaluation select?

sources.title: South San Francisco staff responses to county grand jury ALPR audit findings
sources.summary: Original City staff report proposes responding to the San Mateo County Civil Grand Jury Flock ALPR report. City staff agrees that past ALPR operator audit data were not archived and promises to archive future audits and associated memoranda. Legistar shows this item on the October 28 Consent Calendar with no final action recorded; do not infer implementation, executed vendor protections or council adoption.
sources.proof: File 26-2219, city staff report and grand jury responses, October 28 2026 Council agenda; action row not recorded in Legistar
open_questions: Were the draft grand jury responses formally approved and transmitted by the city?
Have raw operator audit exports and explanatory memos actually been preserved since the response?

sources.title: Proposed South San Francisco resolution approving Flock audit grand jury responses
sources.summary: Official city Legistar resolution 26-2220 would approve the city's response to the county grand jury findings about Flock ALPR oversight, auditing and governance. The resolution was listed October 28; public Legistar final-action field remains blank. A city meeting transcript indicates a council vote, but a final signed adopted resolution or updated Legistar action was not independently obtained; no implementation or contract amendment is inferred.
sources.proof: File 26-2220, proposed resolution, October 28 2026 meeting; Legistar lists Consent Calendar with no final action
open_questions: Has the City Clerk posted a finalized adopted resolution and certified voting record?
Which specific audit, access and sharing safeguards have been implemented rather than promised?

sources.title: Sacramento District Attorney publishes ALPR database-access directive
sources.summary: The Sacramento County District Attorney's publicly hosted ALPR data-access directive states that its office does not employ or deploy ALPR readers, but may access ALPR data collected by other entities. It requires official law-enforcement purposes, case identifiers for queries, agency-manager authorization and periodic audits. The website's January 9, 2026 timestamp is a page timestamp, not independently verified policy-effective date, proof of Flock data access, or an audit of actual searches.
sources.proof: County District Attorney policy webpage, January 9 2026 page timestamp; section III(A-B) no agency-deployed equipment and authorized access, section IV(B,C) authorization and audits
open_questions: Which provider databases does the District Attorney's Office actually have access to, and during what periods?
What is the formal adoption or last-amendment date of the published directive, and are periodic audit reports publicly available?
